blocks.text: The depot report describes day-to-day operations through distinct roles and recurring routines: shift leads inspect operational areas each morning, drivers collect routes and scan parcels, and supervisors write weekly delay summaries. These routines recur across the listed depots, alongside local changes or disruptions such as staffing changes, equipment changes, or weather impacts.

The release process organizes work into three gates. It identifies Alice as the Build owner and Bob as the Deploy owner; Build includes compiling sources and running unit tests, while Deploy restarts workers one at a time.

Both files present work as structured and assigned, but at different levels: the depot report emphasizes recurring operational roles and routines, while the release process emphasizes staged release work, named stage owners, and a controlled deployment sequence. The depot report does not describe release gates or build steps; the release process does not describe depot-style daily inspections, route collection, or weekly delay summaries.

evidence_gaps: The release process says there are three gates, but the evidence only details Build and Deploy; it does not identify or explain the third gate.
